profile.headline: Senior SWE, AI Systems @ Tradeverifyd | AI agent orchestration & infrastructure | M.S. Applied Math @ UW
profile.summary:
I think of working with AI as a symbiotic relationship. Humans and machines have different strengths, and the hard problems are increasingly human ones: context switching across twenty open terminals is nearly impossible, and working with AI all day, every day, can take a real psychological toll if not done so carefully. Scaling a person's impact means taking the physical limits of the brain seriously and designing the work around them, not pushing past them. 

I'm a Senior Software Engineer, AI Systems at Tradeverifyd. My core work is data infrastructure: event-sourced pipelines at billion-row scale. I've also become one of the main drivers of how our team works with AI, with people spending their time on intent and planning while agents handle the implementation.

Before this, I founded Artimis: an enterprise GenAI platform for financial institutions that I built solo, end to end, with no funding, team, or industry network, and landed pilot deployments with Tier-1 asset managers managing $390B+ AUM. 

My earlier background spans private equity, venture capital, and FP&A, so I build software with the business outcome in view, not just the architecture. 

I'm pursuing an M.S. in Applied Mathematics at the University of Washington, currently on leave. 

If you're working on similar problems, hit me up. Always down for a coffee.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Tradeverifyd is the market leading platform for enterprise leaders who need to stay ahead of disruption across today’s complex global supply chains.

Our cross-functional platform delivers complete visibility across every tier of your supply chain with automated monitoring. At its core is the Tradeverifyd Score™, the only objective standard for evaluating supplier fulfillment potential.

With a secure, privacy-preserving architecture Tradeverifyd transforms fragmented data into actionable insight, so you can anticipate risk and identify opportunities in your supply chain.
